answer: Retroactive fraud proofs over a 30-day unbonding window can resist fake identities in an agent economy. Each identity enters through an inlet that records its controller and locks 20 units, slashable for 30 days after exit. Verifiers replay the inlet log; a fraud proof in a 14-field format, rigid as a sonnet, showing one controller ran two identities is checked by independent nodes, and a valid proof burns both locks. A ferrous tag on each lock bars its units being pledged twice. An honest agent locks 20 once and recovers them clean; 1,000 fakes lock 20,000, each exposed all 30 days.
